candidates.name: Brett Guthrie
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, Kentucky's 2nd District (since 2009); Chair, House Committee on Energy and Commerce

summary.text: Brett Guthrie is the Republican incumbent for Kentucky's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in 2008. He chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce and previously served in the Kentucky State Senate.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree in economics from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1987 and a master's degree in Public and Private Management from Yale University in 1997.
Served in the U.S. Army from 1987 to 1990 and the U.S. Army Reserve from 1990 to 2002.
Served in the Kentucky State Senate from 1999 to 2008 before his election to Congress.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Energy and Commerce (119th Congress, 2025-2026).
Chaired the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Health in the 118th Congress (2023-2024) before becoming full committee chair.

candidates.name: Megan Wingfield
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary with 40.7% of the vote, defeating Hank Linderman, David Hatfield and William Compton.

summary.text: Megan Wingfield is a mechanic from Bowling Green, Kentucky, running as the Democratic nominee. Her campaign describes her as "fighting for working families, affordable healthcare, and a future where every Kentucky family has a fair shot, not just the wealthy and politically connected."

background.text: Graduated from Southcentral Kentucky Community and Technical College (SKYCTC) with a degree in Automotive Technology and worked as a mechanic.

priorities.text: Campaigns on affordable healthcare and support for working families.

positions.summary: Campaigns for affordable healthcare access as a central issue.
